patterns: how to clarify what someone means
do you mean vs what do you mean
entries.answer: To clarify is to make something understandable that was not, and it is a different move from asking again, because the speaker is conceding that the problem was the wording rather than the listener. The useful phrases almost all involve checking instead of guessing, being do you mean, so what I am hearing is, and when you say that, do you. The common failure is filling a silence with an assumption, which sounds confident and is routinely wrong.

patterns: how to ask a good follow-up
entries.answer: A follow-up question is one that comes from what was just said rather than from a prepared list, and it is the clearest available signal that somebody is actually listening. It works because it takes a specific detail and builds on it, so what made you choose that, and how does that compare. The alternative is the scripted sequence, which produces answers nobody particularly wanted to give. Preparation flattens a conversation, and the second question is where it shows.

patterns: why do people ask rhetorical questions
entries.answer: A rhetorical question is asked for effect rather than for an answer, and the effect is usually to make a statement look open when it is not. What do we care what they think requires no reply, and anybody who supplies one has misunderstood the move. They appear constantly in argument and in advertising, and the giveaway is that the question already contains its own answer in the wording of the setup.

patterns: what does it mean to probe
entries.answer: Probing is asking one level deeper than the comfortable answer, and the skill is noticing when the person has signalled they would rather not. Done well it is how a real conversation happens; done badly it is an interrogation, and the difference is entirely in whether the person is allowed to stop. The practical guard is to ask once more and then drop it, since a second follow-up after resistance is pressure rather than interest.

patterns: when do you use a question mark
is a question mark a question
entries.answer: A question mark is punctuation that has become the main way English signals a question, because English word order does not reliably do that job on its own. A question mark at the end of a statement is often heard as friendly curiosity, which is why a sentence like you are coming is genuinely ambiguous. A full stop makes it sound like a question instead, and using both together is ambiguous enough that careful writers avoid it.

entries.answer: Curiosity is the wish to know something, and the word is neutral about whether the person would benefit from knowing. That neutrality is what separates it from concern, which assumes it matters, and from snooping, which assumes it is not their business. For conversation the useful distinction is that curiosity asks about what the other person is willing to talk about, so the signal to watch is what they volunteer rather than what they end up answering.
